records.category: anti-corruption case against a deputy governor over bank supervision and unpaid tax
records.people: Bo Bo Nge (deputy governor of the Central Bank of Myanmar, appointed by the NLD government in 2017); the military-backed Anti-Corruption Commission; Open Society Foundation Myanmar (named in the charges)
records.summary: Bo Bo Nge was a deputy governor of the Central Bank of Myanmar, appointed by the National League for Democracy government in 2017, and was detained on the day of the February 2021 coup. In May 2022 the junta-backed Anti-Corruption Commission charged him with failing to tax donations from the Open Society Foundation and with failing to monitor foreign exchange management and the banking and accounting departments. The commission put the losses at 102 million kyats (U.S. $48,500) in stamp duty, 360 million kyats (U.S. $171,000) in tax not collected on a U.S. $5 million deposit by OSF-Myanmar, and 655 million kyats (U.S. $312,000) in tax lost by not placing a U.S. $350 million loan in a higher-interest account. A court convicted him of mismanagement of banks trading foreign currency after what Radio Free Asia described as a months-long secret trial, and sentenced him to 20 years in prison; RFA reported the sentence on 16 December 2022. The report names no specific statute for the charge or the sentence. No statement from Bo Bo Nge, his family or his lawyer appears in the report; information about the trial came from sources close to his family. Sean Turnell, a former economic adviser to Aung San Suu Kyi, said Bo Bo Nge "is a great guy who was fighting against corruption and pushing for reform." The accusations concern the central bank's own supervisory and tax conduct and name its own deputy governor, so the bank and its official are the subject of the finding, not the body making it.
records.source_title: Myanmar junta sentences former Central Bank official to 20 years in prison (Radio Free Asia, 16 December 2022)

notes:
ROUND 53, corruption row, 29 target countries. 24 searches/fetches used. One record filed (MMR). Everything else is a documented blank with the primary source named. Every negative below rests on a page or PDF actually opened unless it says "titles only".

FILED (1)
MMR Myanmar - Bo Bo Nge, deputy governor, charged May 2022 by the junta-backed Anti-Corruption Commission, convicted and sentenced to 20 years, reported by RFA 16 December 2022. Passes the round-52 test: the central bank's own deputy governor and the bank's own supervisory and tax conduct are the subject. Caveat for the main session: the prosecuting body is the military junta's commission and the trial was closed, so the case is a junta prosecution of an NLD appointee; status recorded as "convicted" because a conviction stands and nobody has been cleared. A second outlet (centralbanking.com, "Myanmar sentences ex-deputy governor to 20 years", node 7954023) carries the same facts but is paywalled and was not opened.

CHECKED AND NOT FILED - PRIMARY SOURCES OPENED
FJI Fiji - Parliament of Fiji, "Consolidated Review Report of the Auditor General 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, Audit Report on Statutory Authorities, Independent Bodies and Commissions" (parliament.gov.fj, posted November 2025). Opened and searched: the Reserve Bank of Fiji appears nowhere in it - not in the entity list, the findings or the acronyms. The report covers 12 entities with findings (for example the National Council for Persons with Disabilities and the Sugar Industry Tribunal). For a record to exist, the Auditor-General's separate audit of the Reserve Bank's own accounts would have to be published with a qualification or a fraud note; the consolidated parliamentary review does not carry one. The 1990s National Bank of Fiji collapse remains the most likely place for a supervisory-failure finding against the Reserve Bank, but the surviving public material is academic (Emerald, "Public sector accountability failure in an emerging economy: the case of the National Bank of Fiji") and was not opened within budget.

BRB Barbados - Barbados law courts primary judgment opened in full: "Delisle Worrell v The Minister of Finance" (barbadoslawcourts.gov.bb, March 2017). This is a clean negative on the test and should be recorded as such so a future round does not re-open it. Governor DeLisle Worrell's appointment was revoked in February 2017, but the Minister's stated ground was that the relationship with the Minister and the Central Bank's Board "had irretrievably broken down" (para 12), with termination under the notice clause of the 2014 appointment instrument (paras 9, 24). The judgment sets out NO allegation of misconduct, dishonesty or misbehaviour. The Court of Appeal dismissed Worrell's appeal on 3 March 2017 and awarded the Minister costs. A dismissal on a contractual notice clause after a governance row is not a corruption or misconduct finding, so no record.

PSE Palestine - State Audit and Administrative Control Bureau (ديوان الرقابة المالية والإدارية) annual report for 2020, PDF opened. The Palestine Monetary Authority does appear, but as the CREDITOR: the Bureau's qualified opinion on the Ministry of Finance's closing accounts faults the Ministry for not disclosing an amount owed to the Monetary Authority, 2,130,918 dinars. The finding is against the Ministry of Finance, not the Monetary Authority, so it fails the test. For a record, the Bureau would have to publish a chapter auditing the PMA itself; the 2020 report does not.

HTI Haiti - Cour Superieure des Comptes et du Contentieux Administratif, "Rapport sur quinze ans de finances publiques" (cscca.gouv.ht), opened twice including the box "Encadre 1: Incoherences dans la comptabilisation du financement monetaire". The Court finds that the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti report DIFFERENT monetary-financing figures: for 2019-2020 the Ministry shows none while the BRH reports about 42.9 billion gourdes; for 2020-2021 the Ministry records zero against nearly 49.2 billion gourdes at the BRH; for 2022-2023 the Ministry records nil against 17.25 billion. The Court says these divergences, "parfois d'une ampleur considerable", cast doubt on "la sincerite et la fiabilite des comptes publics" - but it attributes the mismatch to how the GOVERNMENT's accounts record the financing and makes no finding against the BRH. Not filed on the test. This is close, though: if a later CSCCA or IMF safeguards document states that the BRH's own records or its lending to the Treasury breached the law or its own statute, that would be filable. The CSCCA PetroCaribe report 2 (31 May 2019) is online at cscca.gouv.ht and was NOT opened - budget. It is the best unexamined Haitian document for this row.

SYC Seychelles - Office of the Auditor General report AR24 (nationalassembly.sc), opened. The Central Bank of Seychelles appears only in Treasury bank-reconciliation items: a Treasury ledger balance of nil against SR489,355 confirmed by CBS on one account at 31.12.2022 (still persisting); two CBS accounts differing from the ledger by SR3.3m in the 2023 report (resolved); 16 CBS accounts holding SR6,726,178 dormant for 3 years (2021 report); and R200.0m held with CBS for monetary policy purposes in 2024. Every one of these is a finding against the Treasury's bookkeeping, with the CBS as the account-holding bank that CONFIRMS the true balance. Fails the test. For a record, the Auditor General would have to audit the CBS itself, or the Anti-Corruption Commission of Seychelles would have to publish a case naming CBS staff.

WSM Samoa - Central Bank of Samoa own Annual Report 2023-2024 (cbs.gov.ws), opened. Source type 4 (a bank reporting its own staff fraud) produced nothing: no fraud, theft, disciplinary case, internal loss or referral to police is disclosed, and the report names an Internal Audit Department and Audit Committee without reporting any matter at the Bank itself. Caveat: the fetch was truncated before Section IX (Central Bank financial performance) and the external auditor's report, so the audit opinion itself was not seen. The Controller and Chief Auditor's own report on the CBS, and the CBS audited financial statements for FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025 (all PDFs at cbs.gov.ws), were not opened and are the obvious next step.

BHS Bahamas - Central Bank of The Bahamas own press release, "Public Update on the Stolen Banknotes", 6 November 2023 (centralbankbahamas.com), opened. It concerns an armoured car robbery on Thursday 2 November 2023 reported to the Central Bank by a COMMERCIAL bank; the Central Bank states it "was not exposed to the incident" and merely circulated serial numbers to authorities and banks. Not the central bank's money and not its staff: fails the test. No suspects, staff, contractors or amounts are named.

OMN Oman - Oman Daily, "استرداد 6 ملايين ريال المختلسة من البنك.. وإدانة المتهمين" (3 July 2022), opened on the strength of a State Audit Institution search. The 6 million rials were embezzled from Oman Arab Bank, not the Central Bank of Oman, and the article does not mention the Central Bank at all. Not filed. Oman's State Audit Institution (جهاز الرقابة المالية والإدارية للدولة) publishes activity notices and conference news but its annual report findings on named institutions were not findable in open search; that office is where a Central Bank of Oman finding would appear if one exists.

EGY Egypt - NEAR MISS, worth one more search by a later round. Two Egyptian outlets were opened on the same June 2018 Administrative Control Authority (الرقابة الإدارية) arrest: parlmany.com (13 June 2018) and soutalomma.com (article 815921). Both describe the arrest of the "مدير قطاع الرقابة والإشراف" - the director of the supervision and oversight sector - at a bank that supervises foreign currency and exchange companies, accused of taking sums of money as bribes from the owner of a private exchange company in return for ignoring its violations, including foreign-currency trading outside legal channels, and of leaking the dates of planned inspections. He was referred to the Public Prosecution. In Egypt only the Central Bank of Egypt supervises exchange companies, so this is very likely a CBE official - but NEITHER article names the institution, both say only "أحد البنوك" (one of the banks), and the man is unnamed. Not filed, because the rule is that the source must state the fact. What would settle it: an Al-Masry Al-Youm, Al-Ahram or Al-Borsa report on the same June 2018 case that prints "البنك المركزي", or a later Public Prosecution or court statement. Egypt's Central Auditing Organization publishes no findings on the CBE in open search.

DNK Denmark - JUDGEMENT CALL, flagged rather than filed; the main session may want to overrule me. Realtid.se (16 August 2023), opened: the Copenhagen City Court convicted a 53-year-old Russian citizen of attempted gross fraud and forgery for emailing Danmarks Nationalbank and appearing at the bank in person, claiming to represent an investment company and using forged documents, trying to make the bank pay out or transfer 3.5 billion US dollars (put at nearly 38 billion Swedish kronor). He got three years in prison, accepted the sentence and is to be expelled; he was arrested on 21 October 2022. I did not file it: no Nationalbank employee was involved, nothing was paid out, and the bank's staff grew suspicious and called the police - which makes it the same shape as the cases rejected at round 52, a central bank doing the detecting rather than being the subject of a finding. If the row is meant to include an outsider's fraud ATTEMPT on central bank money, this is the record to add and the URL is good. Separately, Denmark's Rigsrevisionen was not reached within budget, and the financial supervisor Finanstilsynet is a separate agency and so out of scope by the brief's own rule.

ARM Armenia - one Armenian-language search (Central Bank employee, corruption, criminal case). Titles only: results were a Central Bank statement on banking secrecy and unrelated company embezzlement cases, nothing naming Central Bank of Armenia staff. Armenia's Audit Chamber (Հաշվեքննիչ պալատ) publishes its reports on its own site and was NOT reached - that is the untried primary source for Armenia.

SLV El Salvador - one Spanish search pairing Banco Central de Reserva with the Corte de Cuentas and the Fiscalia. Titles only: all results concerned municipalities, a former minister and the Corte de Cuentas' own internal problems; none named the BCR. The Corte de Cuentas de la Republica publishes its audit reports and its "juicios de cuentas" rulings on its own site; those were not reached and are the next step.

SDN Sudan - one Arabic search pairing بنك السودان المركزي with the Auditor General's report. Titles only, and every result was a CBoS economic-statistics PDF, not an audit finding. Sudan's Auditor General (المراجع العام) does not appear to publish its annual reports in open, indexable form, and the war has stopped parliamentary scrutiny. Already noted in earlier rounds: the February 2020 dismissal of the CBoS board by an anti-corruption committee came with no stated reason or finding, so it is not filable.

NOT REACHED WITHIN BUDGET - no new search was spent, and the earlier rounds' blanks stand
CAN Canada, SGP Singapore, UZB Uzbekistan, TLS Timor-Leste, ABW Aruba, BHR Bahrain, BMU Bermuda, BRN Brunei, COM Comoros, CPV Cabo Verde, DJI Djibouti, ERI Eritrea, QAT Qatar, SAU Saudi Arabia, BLZ Belize.
One note on TLS: the Portuguese search for the Camara de Contas and the Banco Central de Timor-Leste returned almost entirely Brazilian results about the Banco Central do Brasil and the Banco Master; the Camara de Contas' own site (and Lao Hamutuk, which archives Petroleum Fund documents) was not reached, and RTP reported Timorese opposition warnings about limits placed on the Camara de Contas' oversight - which is itself a reason the row may stay blank.
On BLZ: the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council vein was already worked in an earlier round; [2011] UKPC 36 has the Central Bank of Belize acting AS regulator, which fails the test.

WHAT THE NEXT ROUND SHOULD DO ON THIS ROW
1. Open the central bank's OWN audited financial statements, not the annual report narrative - the auditor's report and the "losses and write-offs" or "contingencies" notes. The Samoa, Seychelles and Bahamas banks all publish these as separate PDFs and I only reached narrative text.
2. Supreme audit institutions that publish on their own sites and were never opened: Armenia's Audit Chamber, El Salvador's Corte de Cuentas, Timor-Leste's Camara de Contas, Haiti's CSCCA PetroCaribe report 2, Oman's State Audit Institution.
3. One targeted Egyptian search to name the institution in the June 2018 exchange-company bribery case. That is the single closest thing to a new record found this round.
4. Do not re-run plain "<country> central bank corruption" on any of these 29. Five rounds have now done it.
